turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Sure! Let me work through one example first.
I need a pen. My friend needs a pen.
"My friend" is one person, like "he" or "she", so I add -s: "needs".
The rule in one line: after he, she, it or one person, add -s to the verb.
Right: She opens the window every morning. Wrong: She open the window every morning.

Now you try. Write the correct form:
My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
